text.p: Shares in electronics retailer Dixons Group Plc slipped on Wednesday after investors decided to take profits following half-year results which met most analysts' expectations.

The shares were 4p lower at 534p by 0854 GMT after initially rising to a high of 544p. "Profits were at the top end of expectations and though sales have come off slightly in current trading, that was expected by most people," said one industry analyst. "But bearing in mind the sort of out-performance we've seen lately, the shares are running into some profit-taking."
Shares in Dixons rose by 40 percent in 1996 compared with 11.6 percent growth in the FTSE 100 index overall.

"People seem unwilling to chase the shares any higher," said one trader. "Sometimes its better to travel than to arrive." One analyst pointed to the lack of any positive surprises in Dixons first-half results and current trading statement.

"Anyone that's held Dixons over the last year has made money out of it.." he said. "I don't think analysts will be rushing to increase forecasts from this..so in the absense of any positive surprises the shares have come off slightly."

Dixons said first-half profits had risen 53 percent in the first half of the year to 57.5 million stg, against analysts' forecasts of 54-57 million stg. An interim dividend of 2.4p was slightly below consensus expectations of 2.5p.

Dixons said like-for-like sales growth over the Christmas trading period was eight percent, falling below the previous year's 11 percent. Gross margins were similar to year-on-year levels after increasing slightly in the first half.
